title: Commercial Self Promotion | AXIOMA: a science deckbuilder is live on Steam for wishlists
author: Typical-Instance-376
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev — I'm Samuel, the developer and publisher behind Quanta — Private Tutoring, based in Brazil. AXIOMA is an upcoming strategy deckbuilder that turns Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics into card combinations: build formulas and molecules, arrange scientist jokers with position-dependent effects, and tune your deck between encounters. It includes a Classic mode, guided tutorials, and interface text in Brazilian Portuguese, English, Spanish, Russian, and Simplified Chinese.



AI disclosure from the Steam page: generative AI assisted the creation of fixed scientific illustrations, scientist portraits, felt textures, card-pack art, text, and translations. These are static assets included with the game; there is no live AI generation during play. I'm sharing this directly because AXIOMA is a commercial game and these AI-assisted assets were part of its workflow.



The Steam page is live for wishlists. Planned release: October 12, 2026. It is not available for pre-purchase at this time:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5308770/AXIOMA/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5308770/AXIOMA/)



For developers working with AI-assisted, rules-heavy games: what review workflow do you use to catch formula, terminology, or localization mistakes before release? I'd like to compare practical QA approaches and can answer questions about the fixed-asset workflow.
